column1: # One row per cell of (name class × collision shape × use position ×
# polarity) that the model in docs/namespaces-design.md makes meaningful.
# `tests/namespace_matrix.sh` fails when a row has neither a fixture nor
# a written reason, so coverage stops depending on anyone's judgement
# Columns: class <TAB> shape <TAB> position <TAB> polarity <TAB> fixture-or-reason <TAB> axes
# The fifth column is either a directory under
#   N/A: <reason>    — the cell cannot be expressed in the language
#   TODO             — a real gap; the gate fails on these
# The sixth column lists the execution axes the row's fixtures run on,
# comma-separated; `-` on N/A rows. This is the ONLY place the corpus
# harness reads its fixture lists from — the `test-namespace-collisions*`
# targets in stage2/Makefile derive them through
# `tests/namespace_matrix_axes.sh <axis>` — so a fixture counted here is
# a fixture executed. Every fixture row carries at least one axis with a
#   c           whole-program C build, stdout vs main.out.expected
#   asan        C build under ASAN+UBSAN, gated on sanitizer diagnostics
#   neg         must fail to compile; stderr contains main.err.expected line 1
#   diag        every line of DIAG.expected is a stderr substring (exit ignored)
#   testsym     `kai test`; main.test.expected line 1 is an output substring
#   check       `kai check`; main.check.expected line 1 is an output substring
#   modular     reserved for the modular build axis; no harness reads it yet
# Each label requires the golden it names to be on disk.
# A cell carries at least TWO fixtures. One example proves the shape
# reproduces once, which is how a cell goes green while its variants stay
# untested — the single fixture is always the benign arrangement, because
# that is the one you reach for first. A cell that genuinely admits only
# one arrangement writes `shallow: <reason>` in the polarity column.
# Adding a class to §2 of the design means adding its rows here.
